articles.title: Treaty limiting US, Russian nuclear weapons expiring as leaders mull what's next
articles.summary: The last major nuclear arms control treaty between the U.S. and Russia, New START, has expired, ending decades of agreements limiting deployable nuclear weapons. This development raises significant concerns about global strategic stability and could lead to an unchecked arms race. For SSB aspirants, understanding this shift in international relations and its defence implications is crucial.

articles.title: Carney’s government is cutting hundreds of environment and science jobs. Here’s what that means for Canadians
articles.summary: Canadian scientists monitoring environmental health, extreme weather, and industrial disasters are at risk of federal job cuts. This decision could significantly impact Canada's capacity to protect its citizens and environment from future challenges, raising concerns about the nation's ability to adapt to climate change and effectively prepare for disasters. The potential cuts highlight a broader debate on government priorities and scientific investment.

articles.title: New Start’s expiration will make the world less safe – even if it doesn’t spark another nuclear arms race
articles.summary: The New Start nuclear arms control treaty between the US and Russia is set to expire on February 4, opening a period of great power uncertainty. This development raises concerns about a potential new global arms race, highlighting the complexities of international security and strategic stability for SSB aspirants.

articles.title: How plans for Trump International hotel in Belgrade unravelled
articles.summary: A city's iconic bomb-damaged defence ministry complex, known as Generalstab, which remained semi-functional despite its state, is set to be replaced. This significant architectural and historical landmark, once a powerful symbol, will make way for new developments. For SSB aspirants, this highlights urban renewal efforts affecting national defence infrastructure, representing both progress and the end of a wartime relic.

articles.title: Mickey Lolich death draws memories from Detroit Tigers greats
articles.summary: Legendary Detroit Tigers pitcher Mickey Lolich passed away on February 4th at 85. The famed 'lefty from Oregon' had a remarkable 16-year MLB career, including 13 seasons with the Tigers. A three-time All-Star, Lolich was a pivotal figure in baseball history, known for his impactful contributions to the sport.

articles.title: Mixed emotions among Palestinians as Rafah crossing partially reopens
articles.summary: The Rafah crossing between Egypt and war-torn Gaza has partially reopened, allowing a small number of Palestinians to return to their homes. Emotional crowds gathered, expressing immense joy at the limited border access. This development underscores the critical humanitarian situation and the longing for stability amidst the ongoing regional conflict, highlighting the impact of border policies on civilian populations.
